description: I am a Solo developer who builds real-world software. We're tackling Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots: merging NASA's two fire-detecting sensors into one consistent record of fire events, demoed as a Telegram alert bot that sends one warning per real fire. Clear plan, working prototype goal. Looking for: remote sensing/GIS, Python data science, web maps (Leaflet), and design/video storytelling. All levels welcome!
summary:
Ghana Fire Calendar is a web app that turns 25 years of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent burning activity calendar for any area of Ghana: the whole country, any of its 16 regions or 260 districts, or a shape the user draws on the map.
Raw hotspot counts jump in 2012. More burning didn't cause the jump: VIIRS started then, and it sees more and smaller fires than MODIS. We put both sensors on a common 0.025° grid and count active cell-days. Then we fit monthly MODIS-to-VIIRS factors over the years both sensors flew, which gives one unbroken record from 2000 to today with about 3% yearly error. VIIRS is the reference because it continues after MODIS ends.
The app shows when the fire season starts, peaks and ends, flags unusual months against the normal, compares regions, gives a 12-month outlook with a tested error range, and updates every day. It shows that 2025/26 was Ghana's lowest fire season on record (38% below normal), with the season moving from north to south. This helps fire services, land managers and researchers plan.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Pick an area of Ghana (the country, a region, a district, or a rectangle or polygon you draw) and the app shows its burning activity calendar from Nov 2000 to today:

  • Calendar heatmap of monthly fire activity, with unusual months flagged against the normal
  • Fire season dates (start, peak, end) for every season, plus a daily view of this year against the normal
  • "One record from two sensors" chart: raw MODIS, raw VIIRS and the harmonized line together, so you can see the fix
  • Map modes: regions, burning hotspots, change against normal, and a weekly "Play season" animation
  • Regions compared: season timing and change for all 16 regions
  • Outlook: 12-month forecast with a range taken from backtesting (error ~10%, against ~15% for just using the normal)
  • Every chart has a table view and can be saved as an image; data can be exported as CSV; links can be shared

HOW IT WORKS (HARMONIZATION)

1. Download the NASA FIRMS standard archives (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS S-NPP 375 m), plus near-real-time data for the latest days. That's 4.2 million hotspots for Ghana.

2. Keep only vegetation fires with nominal or high confidence, the same quality bar for both sensors.

3. Snap detections to a 0.025° grid and count "active cell-days" rather than raw pixels. This removes most of the effect of VIIRS's smaller pixels.

4. In the overlap years (2012 onward), fit one MODIS-to-VIIRS factor per calendar month. Use separate Terra-only factors before Aqua's data starts (July 2002), and mark those months as lower confidence.

5. Build one continuous VIIRS-equivalent record: scaled MODIS before 2012, VIIRS after. Yearly error is about 3.3%. Both raw series stay available.

6. Fire years start at the quietest point of the year (~1 July), so each dry season stays in one piece.

FINDINGS

  • Ghana's season runs ~27 Nov to 15 Mar and peaks ~4 Jan. It moves north to south (Upper East peaks ~23 Nov, Central ~18 Apr).
  • 2021–25 burned 28% less than 2003–11. Greater Accra shows no decline.
  • 2025/26 was the lowest season on record (−38%), below normal in all 16 regions. Savannah, Northern, Bono East and Bono account for 68% of the national drop.

IMPACT

Fire services can see when their district's critical period starts. Land managers can time controlled burns and check whether a season is unusual. Researchers get a long-term record that doesn't break when MODIS retires.

TOOLS

Python, DuckDB + Parquet (data pipeline and queries), FastAPI (API, 49 automated tests), HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Leaflet (map and drawing tools), Apache ECharts (charts), Docker + Caddy on a VPS, GitHub Actions (tests and automatic deploys), and a daily data refresh.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

We count cell-days instead of pixels so the two sensors can be compared fairly. VIIRS is the reference because MODIS is near the end of its mission. Uncertainty is shown openly (lower confidence before Aqua, backtested forecast ranges). Areas with low activity get no season dates, so the app doesn't report false patterns. The site works on phones and in dark mode, and the method is explained in full on the site.

Code (MIT): https://github.com/sonnetechgh-lang/nasa-hotspot-harmonizer

Method: https://harmonizer.10xvibecode.org/method.html
